classifiedFindings.title: PhusdMinterRepoint incompatible with the LIVE 4-field phUSD minter (7-field decode + setMaxMintPerDay absent) — preview reverts before any mutation; YS-12 remediation cannot complete

classification.assetImpact: NONE direct. No asset theft or loss path. The phUSD minter is architecturally immune to the story-060 over-credit bug (mint() = amount x exchangeRate x decimalAdjust; never reads principalOf/totalBalanceOf; no redemption/burn path — run-12 633f3485 scoped analysis). The script cannot move user funds; the worst it leaves is a stale principalOf on the evacuated old strategy (~13,817 DOLA / ~11k USDC) that is the minter's own position, not stolen.
classification.functionAvailabilityImpact: YS-12 minter repoint cannot complete against live mainnet state. Two sub-cases: (default, wired/preview-gated) clean preview revert in the 7-tuple decode of a 4-word return -> NOTHING mutates -> minter stays pointed at the evacuated old strategies = STATUS QUO already classified LOW in run-12. (worse) operator HAND-BROADCASTs the unwired script tx-by-tx (NatSpec still says --skip-simulation): setClient + registerStablecoin land, then setMaxMintPerDay reverts (selector absent) -> minter left half-repointed with per-day cap potentially stuck at 0 -> mint DoS for DOLA/USDC phUSD.
attackPath: Not an external-attacker path. Operator-facing footgun.
1. Operator runs the YS-12 remediation per its NatSpec (which prescribes --skip-simulation, unwired, not in the automated suite).

2. Against the live minter 0x435B..77E5 (older 4-field StablecoinConfig, no setMaxMintPerDay) the preflight 7-tuple decode reverts with empty data BEFORE any mutation (fork-confirmed). Default: nothing changes, status quo preserved.

3. If instead the operator hand-broadcasts tx-by-tx past the preflight, setClient(V2)+registerStablecoin(token,V2,...) land (selectors present), then setMaxMintPerDay reverts (selector absent), leaving the minter config moved to V2 but the per-day cap not restored (possibly 0) = half-repointed + mint DoS.
classification.likelihood: Medium-low. Default path is reverts-safe and benign (status quo). The harmful (half-broadcast) outcome requires an operator to deliberately hand-broadcast an UNWIRED script tx-by-tx, off the preview-gated suite, past a revert — a deliberate off-script action.
classification.assumptions: Harmful state assumes the operator hand-broadcasts the unwired script rather than running it via the (non-existent) wired/preview-gated path and stopping at the clean revert.
classification.externalRequirements: Manual off-script hand-broadcast of the unwired script (NatSpec --skip-simulation). Continued phUSD minting demand on DOLA/USDC for the routing/DoS impact to bite.

classifiedFindings.justification: C4 Medium, NOT High. High requires assets stolen/lost/compromised via a valid no-hypothetical path; the immune-minter analysis forecloses any theft or unbacked-mint, and the default failure is a clean pre-mutation revert that merely preserves an already-Low status quo (run-12 633f3485). The genuinely-new harm is a mint-DoS / half-repointed config in the half-broadcast case — a protocol-function/availability impact with a stated external requirement (manual off-script hand-broadcast), which is the textbook Medium ceiling. It is a Law-3 non-obvious footgun: a competent non-malicious operator running the remediation script would be surprised to brick minting / land a half-repoint. Below-Medium (Low) was considered and rejected only because the half-broadcast mint-DoS is a concrete function impact on a live mint path, not merely state-handling; High was rejected on the absence of any asset-loss path. Safe-config guidance: reconcile the script to the live 4-field minter ABI (drop the maxMintPerDay save/restore + setMaxMintPerDay calls — the live minter has no per-day cap), add a config-word-count preflight that aborts with a clear 'wrong minter version' message, wire it as an npm key so it inherits the story-062 preview hard-gate, and remove --skip-simulation from the NatSpec.
relatedFindings: 633f3485 (run-12 YS-12 referral, classified Low — this remediation cannot complete, so that Low residual persists)

classifiedFindings.title: story-062 live-staker pause has no break-glass: a mid-suite halt strands the LIVE original staker (and the unrelated un-migrated USDe pool) paused; unpause reachable only via a fully-successful PostMigrationCleanup

classification.assetImpact: NONE direct. Funds are not at risk; they are frozen, not lost. Owner-recoverable via manual setPauser/unpause out-of-band.
classification.functionAvailabilityImpact: Real user-facing DoS on the LIVE original staker — all stake/withdraw frozen for DOLA, USDC AND the unrelated, un-migrated USDe pool — for the entire duration of any mid-suite halt. Pause is contract-global. The only unpause path (PostMigrationCleanup ~329 + pauser-restore ~342) is gated behind ~12 verifications + the solvency invariant, so an incomplete/insolvent migration cannot reach it; there is no standalone reopen script in script/.
attackPath: 1. deploy calls setPauser(OWNER)+pause() on both stakers, including the LIVE original (contract-global pause; freezes USDe pool too).
2. Suite halts mid-way (e.g. the DEDUP-13-002 leg1 withdrawer revert, or any mid-suite mainnet condition — exactly what story-062 was hardening for).
3. Cleanup's unpause is unreachable because the full verify+solvency gate cannot pass on an incomplete migration; no break-glass script exists.
4. Live staker + USDe users remain frozen until the operator completes the entire migration or manually unpauses out-of-band.
classification.likelihood: Medium. Mid-suite halts are a realistic operational scenario (the suite itself currently halts on DEDUP-13-002 and YS-04 before fixups); the impact is bounded by operator response time but unbounded by code.
classification.assumptions: A mid-suite halt occurs after deploy/leg1.
classification.externalRequirements: A halt event (operational); manual out-of-band unpause to recover.

classifiedFindings.justification: C4 Medium. Assets are not at direct risk, but protocol AVAILABILITY of a live contract is impacted (stake/withdraw frozen, including the unrelated USDe pool) with a stated external requirement (a mid-suite halt). Recovery is coupled to full-migration success rather than an independent break-glass, and no standalone reopen script exists — so on failure the freeze window is unbounded by code. This is a Law-3 non-obvious owner footgun: a competent non-malicious operator would not anticipate that pausing the live staker as a migration step leaves no decoupled reopen path (the in-comment rationale only contemplates a SHORT happy-path window). Not High (no fund loss; owner-recoverable). Confirmed Medium. Safe-config guidance: ship a minimal standalone EmergencyUnpauseAndRestorePausers script (reads origPauser/tempPauser from ys-swap-deployments.json, unpauses, restores) decoupled from the migration-complete verifications, and document the live-pool freeze (esp. the unrelated USDe pool) in the runbook.

classifiedFindings.title: cleanup silently SKIPS pauser restoration on the JSON catch-path: live staker unpaused but left with the deployer EOA as pauser; post-assert passes vacuously
classifiedFindings.function: run (origPauser/tempPauser try/catch read + gated setPauser restore)

classification.functionAvailabilityImpact: NONE on availability — the unpause (gated on paused()) still runs and the post-asserts require !paused, so the live staker IS reopened. The defect is purely the wrong pauser ADDRESS (deployer EOA) left installed on the degraded catch-path (JSON missing origPauser/tempPauser keys), with the post-assert checking pauser==recorded only when *Recorded is true -> passes vacuously and does not catch the wrong end state.
attackPath: 1. cleanup runs against a JSON missing origPauser/tempPauser (deploy before hardening, or regenerated/partial JSON).
2. try/catch leaves origPauserRecorded=false; setPauser restore (~342) is gated on that flag -> SKIPPED with only a console warning.
3. unpause runs; post-assert (pauser==recorded gated on *Recorded) is vacuously true.

4. Live staker reopened but emergency-pause authority left as the deployer EOA instead of the governance pauser 0x7c5A8EeF..85a3 — silent privilege/wiring drift, run reported COMPLETE with a buried warning.
classification.likelihood: Low — only the degraded-input (missing-keys) catch-path triggers it; the happy path (JSON present) restored correctly on the fork.
classification.assumptions: Deployments JSON is missing the recorded pauser keys.
classification.externalRequirements: None beyond the degraded JSON input.

classifiedFindings.justification: C4 Low. State-handling / degraded-restore footgun: the staker is reopened (no availability loss, no fund loss), but the wrong pauser role (deployer EOA) is silently left on a live contract while the run reports COMPLETE — a latent centralization/operational drift. Owner-fixable. The vacuously-passing post-assert is a spec/state-handling defect, the archetype of QA/Low. It is a Law-3 non-obvious footgun (operator believes cleanup restored the original pauser) so it is reported, not suppressed, but at honest Low severity. Confirmed Low. Guidance: on the catch path FAIL LOUDLY (revert) rather than warn-and-continue, and make the post-assert unconditional (require pauser != deployer after restore).

classifiedFindings.title: PhusdMinterRepoint Phase B re-seeds the V2 position with the (possibly below-par) recovered amount, no >= principal solvency floor — a pre-existing autopool shortfall is silently carried into V2
classifiedFindings.dependsOn: DEDUP-13-001 (MOOT until the ABI mismatch is fixed — script cannot reach Phase B against the live minter today)

classification.assetImpact: NONE migration-caused. Any shortfall ORIGINATES in the external autopool (pre-existing, below-par at migration time), not from the script. The script's defect is the absence of a solvency floor that would abort rather than carry the shortfall forward — it neither creates nor steals value.
classification.functionAvailabilityImpact: None. If the old autopool is below par when (and if) YS-12 ever runs, the minter's V2-backed principal is re-seeded under its recorded phUSD liability with no abort (recovered < p is warn-only ~258; sole post-verify is principalOf > 0 ~319, no require(recovered >= p)). Owner-visible via the warning.
attackPath: 0. Gated: unreachable until DEDUP-13-001 is fixed (script reverts before Phase B against the live minter).
1. Phase B does withdrawAsOwner(minter, owner, p); recovered = balance delta.
2. If recovered < p (below-par pool) the script WARNS and continues (no revert).
3. noMintDeposit(V2, token, recovered) re-seeds V2 with the short amount; only post-check is principalOf > 0 -> under-collateralized position migrated silently.
classification.likelihood: Low and doubly-gated: conditional on a below-par autopool AND on DEDUP-13-001 being fixed first (today the script cannot even reach Phase B).
classification.assumptions: Old autopool is below par at migration time; ABI mismatch (DEDUP-13-001) resolved.

classifiedFindings.justification: C4 Low. Accounting/spec defect (missing solvency floor on reseed) that is conditional (below-par pool only), owner-visible (warning), migration-faithful in framing (shortfall is pre-existing, not migration-caused), and entirely MOOT until the higher-impact DEDUP-13-001 ABI mismatch is fixed since the script cannot reach Phase B against the live minter. A warn-not-revert on a doubly-gated path with no value creation/theft is the archetype of QA/Low. Confirmed Low. Guidance: add an explicit operator-set tolerance (require(recovered >= p * minRecoveryBps / 10000)) or require post-reseed principalOf >= outstanding phUSD liability, so a material shortfall aborts rather than silently migrates under-collateralization.
classifiedFindings.ledgerAction: new entry, severity=low, status=new, footgun=true, dependsOn=DEDUP-13-001.
